Enjoyable with the right people, fun times have been had, and I still want to play it.

Ever since Back 4 Blood was announced, I have been pretty hyped. I loved both Left 4 Dead games, especially in co-op. Initially when Back 4 Blood came out and got bad reviews I was hesitant, but finally I have made the decision to just buy it and play it with friends in co-op.

To be short, I don’t quite get the bad reviews. I loved Back 4 Blood. In many aspects it’s just like Left 4 Dead but it feels a bit more modern, and has more replay-ability thanks to the deck building, characters with different stats and weapon buying, which makes it more fun to try completely different play styles. It’s still the same old thing, where you walk through various levels from safe room to safe room slaughtering hordes of zombies. That however, doesn’t mean everything is better or perfect.

Let’s go over the good things first. The game is largely similar to the old Left 4 Dead games. It also feels a lot more modern as shooting works better, graphics look a lot better, and sound design is up to modern standards. The game is (in my opinion) also much better in terms of replay-ability. You can now choose out of a set of characters that all have their own things they’re good at. This in combination with the deck building system and the fact that you can actually buy weapons instead of needing to find them, gives you the option to make runs vastly different from each other.

Some things I don’t like as much are first and foremost the act system. At higher difficulties the game requires you to complete multiple levels in order to get checkpoints to start a new run from. This turns the game at times into a quite repetitive flow as you encounter a harder level and you have to replay multiple levels the whole time. There lies my next con, The easy difficulty is way too easy, you blast through the game with 2 fingers in your nose, but 1 difficulty higher is(at times) way too challenging for casual play.

I also personally found “special zombies” to be spawned too much. Where in Left 4 Dead zombies like the boomer, the hunter and the witch were zombies that you encountered at times, here it feels like you encounter them the whole time. Making it less of a “Oh snap” moment. One last thing I didn’t like is that in order to swap cards in your decks, you need to rebuild the whole deck because order of cards matters, and you can’t simply swap one out in the middle of the deck.

Overall, I still did enjoy the game a lot in co-op. It’s fun, plays good and has a campaign that is quite lengthy(Also because you have to replay levels at times). I also liked the card system because it really made me try vastly different play styles.

Gotta love how some people wait till they've clocked over 400 hours and completed the game on every difficulty to give a thumbs down review.
You must've KINDA dug the game to sit in it for 400+ hours, no?
This game is a blast BUT only as fun as the people you play with.
If you do random PUG, then there's always some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tryin to ice skate uphill (collect all the coins).
These maps were not designed to just run through as fast as you can.
There's even a separate spoken line for each character that tells you to "Get back with the group" if you run off alone.
Do they listen?
I think we know the answer to that one.
If you get a good group of people who are familiar with the game, then you will have a damn good time.
Maps are beautiful but could be longer on some parts.
Bots AI could be better but you can still finish it even on Veteran with them.
Only thing missing is dualies.
I'd say it's the perfect "Step Up" from LFD2!

Equally chaotic with friends and random, some of the levels are unique, though some maps have re-runs albeit in different directions. I can expect the game to get better with more cleaners and modes. The card-based perk system and satisfying gun play build upon the superb groundwork of the Left 4 Dead series.
